built: atelier composition on the ink-sketch playbook

decisions.choice: chronostasis — the stopped-clock illusion, and saccadic masking underneath it
decisions.why: universally experienced, genuinely counterintuitive, and it can be PERFORMED by a single still figure and one prop. The ledger forbids repeating the doorway effect's read; this one is about what is absent from the frame rather than about what the character does.

decisions.choice: the page goes blank for two frames, nine times
decisions.why: the device IS the argument. Nothing has to be explained about it; the audience experiences the thing the narration is describing, including once under the exact line that names it.

decisions.choice: one tick per second of clock time, generated from the same function that turns the hand
decisions.why: so the sound cannot drift from the picture. The hang and every blank are silent because dialSeconds() says so, not because they were placed by hand.

decisions.choice: two setups, six cuts, cut on the looks
decisions.why: video four was one continuous shot and said so in writing. Also: a look IS a cut — the figure's head cannot turn, so the edit does the looking.

decisions.choice: cut back to the wide for 30.55-35.90
decisions.why: the close-up ran 21 seconds with only the caption changing, which is the scene-level templating trap the ledger names. The two lines in that window are about him, not about the clock.

decisions.choice: stillness — one still pose for 48 seconds, one turn, one eyebrow
decisions.why: a different motion character from video four's six travelling mocap clips, and true to the subject: nothing is moving except time and the cuts.

decisions.choice: orange = invented time, blue once = the true measure, no red
decisions.why: different roles from video four, where orange was an object and blue was an end-state.

decisions.choice: 'something like a tenth of your waking life', not a figure in minutes
decisions.why: popular accounts quote anything from 40 minutes to 1.5 hours because the arithmetic depends on saccade rate and how suppression is counted. A tenth is defensible at 3-4 saccades/s and ~50ms each, and it is a stronger line.

decisions.choice: built as an atelier composition, not through the 11-stage character-animation pipeline
decisions.why: skills/creative/ink-theater.md declares the style pipeline-exempt. The artifacts that carry information — script, timing, this log, the render report, the source docs — are written; the schema-validated stage checkpoints are not.
